sources: No per-nation sourcing note existed when this nation was first entered in init.rs; the table header recorded only "Transcribed-not-invented: approximate 1990 historical starting conditions".
Figures below are transcribed unchanged from that table. Their origin was not documented at the time and is a known gap in provenance.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.2310%/yr. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 42.382 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, GBR, 1989: US$42381854893.74 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 20 were held and are listed below with their citations; 28 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_packet_internetworking, core_combined_cycle_turbine, comp_risc_superscalar, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. core_packet_internetworking -> NOT HELD (semiconductors-computing said held, telecom-space said not held; resolved to the board that owns the Communications domain, telecom-space).

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 1 cell: ener_seismic_3d_imaging (energy and transport board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below.

granted.source: Route (b), inherited from comp_microprocessor in this file: World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 10.85 PCs per 100, fourth-highest in the series and 4.4x the 1990 World value of 2.45. A commodity 32-bit installed base at that density is 1.0-1.2-micron-generation CMOS running in the economy.

STC (Standard Telephones and Cables) supplied one of the three separately-contracted subsegments of TAT-8, the first transoceanic fibre-optic cable, in service 14 December 1988 - a repeatered single-mode system with submerged regenerators, which is the full conjunction the predicate asks for. STC's optical work descended from Standard Telecommunication Laboratories at Harlow.

Carbon fibre was invented at RAE Farnborough in 1963 (Watt, Phillips and Johnson) and licensed to Courtaulds, Morganite and Rolls-Royce; Courtaulds produced it commercially as Grafil from 1968 and was still producing in 1990, with prepreg from Ciba-Geigy Bonded Structures at Duxford.

Britain's molecular-genetics base was first rank and PCR-capable by 1989: the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology at Cambridge, where Sanger's dideoxy sequencing (1977) and Kohler and Milstein's hybridoma (1975) were done, and the University of Leicester laboratory of Alec Jeffreys, which produced DNA fingerprinting in 1984 and whose casework moved onto amplification-based typing at the end of the decade.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 10.85 PCs per 100, 4.4x the World value of 2.45.
Oracle established a United Kingdom subsidiary within three years of 1982 (Oracle corporate histories, as above). The UK also holds comp_microprocessor at 10.85 PCs per 100.

R3: TACS cellular service opened in the UK on 1 January 1985 (Vodafone), joined by Cellnet on 7 January 1985. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 1,114,000 UK mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990. Separately, BT's System X digital exchange programme and its all-digital trunk network were long established by 1990.

British Telecom committed to nationwide networks on single-mode fibre in 1982 and opened the world's first 140 Mbit/s single-mode optical fibre system between Milton Keynes and Luton in 1984; BT's national optical fibre network went on to render its microwave trunk network obsolete. Europe's first optical cable in a public telephone network had been BT's Martlesham-to-Ipswich route in 1978.

Skynet 4B was launched on 11 December 1988 on the first operational Ariane 4 flight (V27) from Kourou. Skynet 4A, 4B and 4C, manufactured by British Aerospace Dynamics, are described as the first purely British-built satellites. A geostationary military communications satellite of British prime manufacture, flying before the start date.

TACS cellular service opened in the UK on 1 January 1985, when Vodafone launched; Cellnet joined on 7 January 1985. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 1,114,000 UK mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990, the largest in Europe.

LIMB A FAILS and is not used - see this node's note; granted on the named-artefact bar exactly as the first pass ruled the USA cell. LIMB B: the United Kingdom is in the Advanced Set. EVIDENCE E2, a named pre-1990 three-dimensional survey over this nation's acreage: the Strathspey field in the UK sector of the northern North Sea - a tilted, eroded fault block producing from the Brent and Statfjord reservoirs, held by a field group of Texaco, Shell, Esso and Oryx - was covered by a 3-D seismic dataset OF 1985 VINTAGE. The dating is not incidental to the source: the 1985 3-D volume is the baseline against which the field group's 1995-96 vertical-cable survey was measured, and the paper reporting that later survey records the improvement of the vertical-cable data over 'the previous 3D dataset from vintage 1985'. Source: P. Leach, 'Strathspey vertical-cable seismic survey: a North Sea first', Geological Society, London, Petroleum Geology Conference Series (1998). LIMB C SEARCHED: no named, citable fact was found placing the UK Continental Shelf outside 3-D acquisition in the 1980s, and the contrary background is that the North Sea is one of the three provinces named as taking up the technique by the mid-1980s. DISCLOSED LIMIT: this grant rests on ONE named dated survey over one UKCS field, not on a count or a share of UKCS acreage covered by 3-D before 1990, which I could not find published. It is an existence claim and should be read as one.
British Aerospace built the carbon-fibre wing of the EAP demonstrator, first flight 8 August 1986, and the composite wing of the Harrier GR5 in the AV-8B programme.

Rolls-Royce developed the SRR99 single-crystal alloy and carried single-crystal high-pressure turbine blades into the RB211 family through the 1980s, cast in-house at Derby. MODERATE: the alloy and the capability are firm; I have not pinned the exact engine mark and year of first service.

GEC-Marconi AI.24 Foxhunter pulse-Doppler look-down/shoot-down radar, designed and built in the UK for the Tornado F.2/F.3, with radar-equipped aircraft delivered from the mid-1980s and the Stage 1 standard fitted from 1989; Ferranti Blue Vixen pulse-Doppler for the Sea Harrier flying in trials aircraft from 1988; Marconi Martello S713 three-dimensional electronically-scanned-in-elevation surveillance radar in the Improved UK Air Defence Ground Environment from the mid-1980s.

Trafalgar-class SSN, lead boat HMS Trafalgar commissioned 27 May 1983 — the class introduced anechoic tiling and a pump-jet propulsor to Royal Navy service, with raft-mounted machinery. Vanguard-class SSBN laid down from 1986 to the same design practice.

Humulin, recombinant human insulin, was licensed for sale in the United Kingdom in 1982 — the same year as the FDA's 30 October 1982 approval, and by several accounts the first national licence granted anywhere for a genetically engineered medicine. Britain also had a domestic biologics industry by the end of the decade in the Wellcome Foundation and in Celltech, founded at Slough in 1980 as the United Kingdom's national biotechnology company.
WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, United Kingdom, 1990: 84%. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('United Kingdom,GBR,1990,84').

Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half, and Britain invented one of them. Godfrey Hounsfield's EMI scanner made the first computed-tomography scan of a patient at Atkinson Morley's Hospital, Wimbledon, on 1 October 1971. John Mallard's group at the University of Aberdeen produced the first clinically useful magnetic-resonance images of a patient in 1980, on a machine that went into service at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary.

The Felixstowe cargo processing system FCP80 was in operation at Britain's principal container port from 1984 - one of the three earliest port community systems in Europe - and was renamed FCPS in 1990. Piernext (Port de Barcelona), 'The fourth wave of Port Community Systems'; A. Long, 'Port Community Systems', World Customs Journal 3(1).

Scottish Atlantic salmon farming in sea cages: production rose from 600 tonnes in 1980 to 115,000 tonnes by 1998, and the Scottish Fish Farm Production Survey publishes annual Atlantic salmon production and staff by area from 1990 onward (Scottish Government Marine Directorate, Scottish Fish Farm Production Survey data, Tables 32-35; Salmon Scotland, 'Scottish Salmon Farming History'). The industry was operating throughout the 1980s.
